problems.name: HumanEval_108_count_nums
problems.code:
def count_nums(arr)
    arr.count { |num| sum_of_digits(num) > 0 }
end

def sum_of_digits(num)
    digits = num.to_s.chars.map(&:to_i)
    if num < 0
        digits[0] *= -1
    end
    digits.sum
end

require 'test/unit'
class TestHumanEval < Test::Unit::TestCase
  def test_count_nums
    candidate = method(:count_nums)
    assert_equal(0, candidate.call([]))
    assert_equal(0, candidate.call([-1, -2, 0]))
    assert_equal(6, candidate.call([1, 1, 2, -2, 3, 4, 5]))
    assert_equal(5, candidate.call([1, 6, 9, -6, 0, 1, 5]))
    assert_equal(4, candidate.call([1, 100, 98, -7, 1, -1]))
    assert_equal(5, candidate.call([12, 23, 34, -45, -56, 0]))
    assert_equal(1, candidate.call([0, 1]))
    assert_equal(1, candidate.call([1]))
  end
end

problems.name: HumanEval_111_histogram
problems.code:
def histogram(test)
  return {} if test.empty?
  
  letters = test.split(' ')
  counts = Hash.new(0)
  
  letters.each { |letter| counts[letter] += 1 }
  
  max_count = counts.values.max
  counts.select { |_, count| count == max_count }
end

require 'test/unit'
class TestHumanEval < Test::Unit::TestCase
  def test_histogram
    candidate = method(:histogram)
    assert_equal({"a" => 2, "b" => 2}, candidate.call("a b b a"))
    assert_equal({"a" => 2, "b" => 2}, candidate.call("a b c a b"))
    assert_equal({"a" => 1, "b" => 1, "c" => 1, "d" => 1, "g" => 1}, candidate.call("a b c d g"))
    assert_equal({"r" => 1, "t" => 1, "g" => 1}, candidate.call("r t g"))
    assert_equal({"b" => 4}, candidate.call("b b b b a"))
    assert_equal({"r" => 1, "t" => 1, "g" => 1}, candidate.call("r t g"))
    assert_equal({}, candidate.call(""))
    assert_equal({"a" => 1}, candidate.call("a"))
  end
end

    return -1 if n > m

problems.name: HumanEval_87_get_row
problems.code:
# You are given a 2 dimensional data, as a nested arrays,
# which is similar to matrix, however, unlike matrices,
# each row may contain a different number of columns.
# Given lst, and integer x, find integers x in the array,
# and return array of arrays, [(x1, y1), (x2, y2) ...] such that
# each array is a coordinate - (row, columns), starting with 0.
# Sort coordinates initially by rows in ascending order.
# Also, sort coordinates of the row by columns in descending order.
# Examples:
# >>> get_row.call([[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], [1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 6], [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 1]], 1)
# [[0, 0], [1, 4], [1, 0], [2, 5], [2, 0]]
# >>> get_row.call([], 1)
# []
# >>> get_row.call([[], [1], [1, 2, 3]], 3)
# [[2, 2]]
def get_row(lst, x)
coordinates = []

    lst.each_with_index do |row, row_index|
        row.each_with_index do |value, col_index|
            if value == x
                coordinates << [row_index, col_index]
            end
        end
    end

    # Sort by rows ascending, then by columns descending within each row
    coordinates.sort_by { |row, col| [row, -col] }
end
end


require 'test/unit'
class TestHumanEval < Test::Unit::TestCase
  def test_get_row
    candidate = method(:get_row)
    assert_equal([[0, 0], [1, 4], [1, 0], [2, 5], [2, 0]], candidate.call([[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], [1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 6], [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 1]], 1))
    assert_equal([[0, 1], [1, 1], [2, 1], [3, 1], [4, 1], [5, 1]], candidate.call([[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]], 2))
    assert_equal([[0, 0], [1, 0], [2, 1], [2, 0], [3, 2], [3, 0], [4, 3], [4, 0], [5, 4], [5, 0], [6, 5], [6, 0]], candidate.call([[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], [1, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6], [1, 2, 1, 4, 5, 6], [1, 2, 3, 1, 5, 6], [1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 6], [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 1]], 1))
    assert_equal([], candidate.call([], 1))
    assert_equal([], candidate.call([[1]], 2))
    assert_equal([[2, 2]], candidate.call([[], [1], [1, 2, 3]], 3))
  end
end

    freq = Hash.new(0)
    lst.each { |num| freq[num] += 1 }

problems.name: HumanEval_131_digits

def digits(n)
    product = 1
    has_odd = false
    
    while n > 0
        digit = n % 10
        if digit.odd?
            product *= digit
            has_odd = true
        end
        n /= 10
    end
    
    has_odd ? product : 0
end

problems.name: HumanEval_78_hex_key
problems.code:
def hex_key(num)
    primes = Set.new([2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13])
    count = 0
    
    num.each_char do |char|
        case char.upcase
        when 'A'
            count += 1 if primes.include?(10)
        when 'B'
            count += 1 if primes.include?(11)
        when 'C'
            count += 1 if primes.include?(12)
        when 'D'
            count += 1 if primes.include?(13)
        when 'E'
            count += 1 if primes.include?(14)
        when 'F'
            count += 1 if primes.include?(15)
        else
            digit = char.to_i
            count += 1 if primes.include?(digit)
        end
    end
    
    count
end

def how_many_times(string, substring)
    return 0 if string.empty? || substring.empty?
    
    count = 0
    start = 0
    
    while (pos = string.index(substring, start)) != nil
        count += 1
        start = pos + 1
    end
    
    count
end

def largest_prime_factor(n)
  factors = []
  d = 2
  while d * d <= n
    if (n % d).zero?
      factors << d
      n /= d
    else
      d += 1
    end
  end
  factors << n unless n == 1
  factors.max
end

def get_closest_vowel(word)
    vowels = 'aeiouAEIOU'
    
    # Start from the second last character and go backwards to the second character
    (word.length - 2).downto(1) do |i|
        char = word[i]
        prev_char = word[i-1]
        next_char = word[i+1]
        
        # Check if current character is a vowel
        if vowels.include?(char)
            # Check if previous and next characters are consonants
            if !vowels.include?(prev_char) && !vowels.include?(next_char)
                return char
            end
        end
    end
    
    ""
end

problems.name: HumanEval_93_encode

def encode(message)
  vowels = 'aeiouAEIOU'
  result = ''
  
  message.each_char do |char|
    if char.match?(/[a-zA-Z]/)
      # Swap case
      swapped_case = char.swapcase
      
      # Replace vowel with letter 2 places ahead
      if vowels.include?(swapped_case)
        index = vowels.index(swapped_case)
        replacement_index = (index + 2) % vowels.length
        result += vowels[replacement_index]
      else
        result += swapped_case
      end
    else
      result += char
    end
  end
  
  result
end

def check_if_last_char_is_a_letter(txt)
  return false if txt.nil? || txt.empty?
  
  last_char = txt[-1]
  return false unless last_char.match(/[a-zA-Z]/)
  
  # Check if the character before the last one is a space or non-alphabetical
  # If there's no previous character, it means we're dealing with just one letter,
  # which should be considered as part of a word (since there's nothing to separate it from).
  return true if txt.length == 1
  
  prev_char = txt[-2]
  !prev_char.match(/[a-zA-Z]/)
end

def get_max_triples(n)
    # Create the array where a[i] = i * i - i + 1 for i from 1 to n
    a = Array.new(n) { |i| (i + 1) * (i + 1) - (i + 1) + 1 }
    
    count = 0
    
    # Iterate through all possible triples where i < j < k
    for i in 0...n-2
        for j in (i+1)...n-1
            for k in (j+1)...n
                sum = a[i] + a[j] + a[k]
                if sum % 3 == 0
                    count += 1
                end
            end
        end
    end
    
    count
end

def strange_sort_list(lst)
    result = []
    sorted_lst = lst.sort
    left, right = 0, sorted_lst.length - 1
    
    while left <= right
        if result.empty? || result.last == sorted_lst[left]
            result << sorted_lst[right]
            right -= 1
        else
            result << sorted_lst[left]
            left += 1
        end
    end
    
    result
end

    candidate = method(:strange_sort_list)

problems.name: HumanEval_117_select_words
problems.code:
def select_words(s, n)
    return [] if s.empty?
    
    vowels = Set.new(['a', 'e', 'i', 'o', 'u'])
    words = s.split
    result = []
    
    words.each do |word|
        consonant_count = word.downcase.chars.count { |c| c.match?(/[a-z]/) && !vowels.include?(c) }
        result << word if consonant_count == n
    end
    
    result
end

problems.name: HumanEval_11_string_xor
problems.code:
def string_xor(a, b)
    # Ensure both strings are of equal length by padding with leading zeros if necessary
    max_length = [a.length, b.length].max
    a = a.rjust(max_length, '0')
    b = b.rjust(max_length, '0')

    result = ""
    (0...max_length).each do |i|
        # XOR operation: same bits produce 0, different bits produce 1
        if a[i] == b[i]
            result += "0"
        else
            result += "1"
        end
    end

    result
end

    assert_equal("010010", candidate.call("111000", "101010"))
    assert_equal("0", candidate.call("1", "1"))
    assert_equal("0101", candidate.call("0101", "0000"))
  end
end

problems.name: HumanEval_68_pluck
problems.code:
def pluck(arr)
    return [] if arr.empty?
    
    min_even = nil
    min_index = -1
    
    arr.each_with_index do |value, index|
        next unless value.even? && value >= 0
        
        if min_even.nil? || value < min_even
            min_even = value
            min_index = index
        end
    end
    
    return [] if min_even.nil?
    
    [min_even, min_index]
end

    assert_equal([2, 1], candidate.call([4, 2, 3]))
    assert_equal([2, 1], candidate.call([1, 2, 3]))
    assert_equal([], candidate.call([]))
    assert_equal([0, 1], candidate.call([5, 0, 3, 0, 4, 2]))
    assert_equal([0, 3], candidate.call([1, 2, 3, 0, 5, 3]))
    assert_equal([4, 1], candidate.call([5, 4, 8, 4, 8]))
    assert_equal([6, 1], candidate.call([7, 6, 7, 1]))
    assert_equal([], candidate.call([7, 9, 7, 1]))
  end
end

    return [] if array.empty?
    return array.dup.sort if (array.first + array.last).odd?

problems.name: HumanEval_6_parse_nested_parens
problems.code:
def parse_nested_parens(paren_string)
    groups = paren_string.split(' ')
    result = []
    
    groups.each do |group|
        max_depth = 0
        current_depth = 0
        
        group.chars.each do |char|
            if char == '('
                current_depth += 1
                max_depth = [max_depth, current_depth].max
            elsif char == ')'
                current_depth -= 1
            end
        end
        
        result << max_depth
    end
    
    result
end

require 'test/unit'
class TestHumanEval < Test::Unit::TestCase
  def test_parse_nested_parens
    candidate = method(:parse_nested_parens)
    assert_equal([2, 3, 1, 3], candidate.call("(()()) ((())) () ((())()())"))
    assert_equal([1, 2, 3, 4], candidate.call("() (()) ((())) (((())))"))
    assert_equal([4], candidate.call("(()(())((())))"))
  end
end
